findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw shell eggs stored above ready-to-eat foods (string cheese and PB&J sandwiches) in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and the eggs were moved to a separate shelf where they were not above RTE food. Ensure that raw animal products (eggs and meat) are stored below RTE food (prepared produce, deli meat, cheese, beverages).
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed that the ventilation system above the heat dish machine was not functioning, causing excessive steam and heat to accumulate in the dish area. Staff have placed floor fans to ventilate the area, as clean dishes take significant time to air-dry because of the excessive humidity caused by the non-functioning ventilation system. Repair the ventilation system by the next routine inspection to ensure that the ventilation hood system is sufficient in capacity to prevent condensation from collecting on equipment.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.14 Ventilation Hood Systems, Adequacy. Ventilation hood systems and devices shall be sufficient in number and capacity to prevent grease or condensation from collecting on walls and ceilings. [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Observed several dented cans in the dry storage area. The dented cans were removed from service and the PIC was educated. Ensure that food packages are always in good condition to protect the integrity of the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the sanitizer buckets were testing at 0-452 ppm (Lactic Acid; Sink and Surface Cleaner). The sanitizer buckets were remade testing at 704 ppm (Lactic Acid) during the inspection. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always testing at the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the dish machine was testing at 152-153F with a maximum registering thermometer. The facility will be washing and rinsing items inside the dish machine and sanitizing in the tripe sink until the dish machine is serviced. The inspector will follow-up on 12/15/2025 to check that the dish machine is properly sanitizing.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F).

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed single-use utensils stored with the handles and food contact surfaces intermixed. During the inspection the utensils were moved into an upright container with the handles sticking outwards to limit students touching the food contact portions. Ensure the utensils are always stored to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present at the facility. The PIC will be taking the CFPM class. Ensure there is a CFPM present during all hours of operation by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee turned off the faucets with their bare hands after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that not all employees have food handler certificates. All employees who do not have the CFPM certificate must complete basic food handler training. Ensure that all employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth drying on the basin of the triple sink when the inspector arrived. The inspector educated that wet wiping cloths must be stored in chemical sanitizer between uses. The PIC placed the wet wiping cloth in the laundry basket during the inspection. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in chemical sanitizer solution between uses and laundered daily.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that not all employees working have their food handler certificates. One employee stated they took the class but they don’t have a copy of their certificate, and the other three said they have not taken the class. All employees who do not have the CFPM (certified food protection manager) certificate must complete basic food handler training. Ensure that all employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Observed the maximum temperature of the dish machine was 154 F. The dish machine was run several times but the maximum temperature remained too low. The PIC stated they will be getting the dish machine serviced. The facility can still use the dish machine for the wash and rinse cycle, but they must use the triple sink for sanitizing. The sanitizer dispenser at the triple sink tested correctly during the inspection. The inspector will return on 09/06/2024 to ensure that the dish machine is reaching the correct maximum temperature (between 157 and 163 F).

4-501.110: (A) Temperature of the wash solution in spray type warewashers using hot water may not be less than: 165F for stationary rack-single temperature, 150F for stationary rack-dual temperature machine, 160F single tank, conveyor-dual temperature, 150F multitank conveyor-multitemperature. (B) Temperature for wash solution using chemical SANITIZER may not be less than 120F.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed that not all employees have gotten their food handler certification. All food handlers (who do no have the CFPM certification) must complete basic food handling principle training. Ensure that all employees get their food handlers certification by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several moist towels sitting on the wooden countertop where food preparation was occurring. Operator promptly had towel removed while I was in the facility without being instructed to do so. Corrected on site. Ensure that in-use wiping cloths are stored in chemical sanitizing solution when not in immediate use wiping surfaces. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Upon entering the kitchen, inspector observed a covered cup of coffee sitting on the wooden counter top where food preparation was occurring. The cup was promptly removed from the area by direction of the operation without being instructed to do so. Corrected on site. Ensure that personal drinks and other personal items are stored in a designated area away from food preparation and storage areas.

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Observed mice droppings in dry storage and under dishwasher. PIC will clean areas. Ensure evidence of pests are removed in timely fashion. PIC will email proof and frequency of pest control. Reference 6-501.112.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment:
Observed handwashing station in kitchen as well as bathroom handsink to be unable to reach 100F. Hot and cold running water under pressure shall be provided. Repair sink to provide hot (100F) water. 
750-1120 Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: Observed Hot dogs over powdered sugar in the walk in cooler.  Observed sneeze guards to be too high and the food to be sticking out from under the guard. The food is not protected by these sneeze guards. 750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment: Observed the hot water in the hand sink in the kitchen to be not greater than 82F. Hot and cold running water under pressure shall be provided. Repair sink to provide hot water.  750-1120 Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: Observed a large rolling garbage can to be in front of the only hand sink in the kitchen. The can was moved. Provide other smaller garbage for hand towels. 750-1120(b) Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee was observed putting on gloves without first washing hands after exiting the walkin cooler. The employee was later observed turning off the manual faucet without a proper barrier after hands were washed. Handwashing between tasks and proper technique were discussed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.
Always use a paper towel as a barrier to shut off the faucet once handwashing is completed to avoid contamination of freshly washed hands.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sani-buckets were observed at 100ppm quat upon arrival of inspector. Employee noted they were prepared around 730a and are typically changed out at 11a. Solutions were changed and observed at 400ppm quat after being dispensed. Maintain quat solution at 150-400ppm quat per the label instructions for the product being used. Change solutions more frequently if concentration drops below 150ppm and/or if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled.

Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The bottom inside of both microwaves are soiled with food debris. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintain clean.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Floor behind the prep table that is sealed to the wall is soiled. 750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors and maintain free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
WHEN REMODEL: the ceiling tile in the kitchen, dish area, and the restroom are pitted and not smooth and easily cleanable. Replace with smooth and cleanable tiles when remodeling occurs.
750-1210(b) Walls and ceilings in walk-in refrigeration units, food preparation areas, equipment washing areas, and toilet rooms shall be smooth, light-cored, non-absorbant, and easily cleanable. Concrete or pumice block in these locations shall be finished and sealed to provide a cleanable surface.
The ceiling area near the 2 air conditioning units in the kitchen with evidence of dust on tiles and the lights in the kitchen. Clean the lights and ceiling tile.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
